debates.title: Can LLMs natively read and write model weights?
debates.summary: New research showing that large language models can directly interpret and modify raw neural network weights has captured attention across the community. This technique, dubbed weight-space programming, raises questions about how smaller open-weight models compare to frontier systems like GPT-6 Astra.

positions.stance: Demonstrates that smaller open models like Qwen 3.8 27B running locally can also achieve weight-space programming after some runtime.
Describes weight-space programming as a blockbuster capability find that cuts autoresearch out of the recursive self-improvement loop.

debates.summary: As market corrections hit tech stocks and questions mount over the real-world value of AI products, observers are divided on whether current costs outweigh the benefits. This debate highlights the tension between financial reality and the unstoppable pace of AI deployment.

positions.stance: Argues that current AI products are not good enough to justify their high financial and environmental costs.
Maintains that financial market downturns or stock drops will not slow down AI adoption, development, or its long-term trajectory.
